title: Feedback Loops for Logistic Field & Hardware Domain
description: Structured checks for understanding and user feedback during Socratic AI dialogues.

questions.text: Did this explanation of finite state machines help? (yes/no)

next_steps.no: Retry with another anchor or simplify the explanation.

questions.text: Can you explain what a finite state machine is in your own words?

next_steps.positive: Proceed to discuss specific applications of FSMs in hardware design.
next_steps.negative: Clarify the explanation with a different analogy.

questions.text: Does the explanation of FPGA prototyping make sense? (yes/no)

next_steps.no: Try explaining with a different analogy or example.

questions.text: How would you describe FPGA prototyping to someone else?

next_steps.positive: Discuss how FPGAs are used in real-world applications like signal processing or hardware acceleration.
next_steps.negative: Revisit the explanation with more concrete examples.

questions.text: Did the explanation of ASIC design help you understand the concept? (yes/no)

next_steps.yes: Proceed to discuss the ASIC design flow in more detail.
next_steps.no: Provide another example of ASIC design.

questions.text: Can you think of a scenario where an ASIC would be more suitable than an FPGA?

next_steps.positive: Explore the trade-offs between ASICs and FPGAs in terms of cost, performance, and flexibility.
next_steps.negative: Discuss common use cases for ASICs and FPGAs.

questions.text: Did this explanation of hardware verification help? (yes/no)

next_steps.yes: Proceed to discuss different verification methodologies (e.g., simulation, formal verification).
next_steps.no: Provide another analogy or example of verification.

questions.text: Why is verification important in hardware design?

next_steps.positive: Discuss the impact of verification on time-to-market and product reliability.
next_steps.negative: Explain the consequences of skipping verification in hardware design.

questions.text: Did the explanation of Turing machines help you understand the concept? (yes/no)

next_steps.yes: Proceed to discuss the Church-Turing thesis or the relationship between Turing machines and modern computers.
next_steps.no: Provide another analogy or example of Turing machines.

questions.text: How would you explain a Turing machine to a friend?

next_steps.positive: Explore how Turing machines form the foundation of computability theory.
next_steps.negative: Discuss simpler models of computation and their limitations.
